proposed_h1: AMC Yellow Ticket Deals: Movie Tickets from $5.29 – Save 20% vs. National Average
proposed_highlights: Movie ticket valid for any standard 2D film at AMC Theatres nationwide (excludes CA, NY, NJ)
Redeem online or at any AMC box office – 7 days a week, all showtimes (evenings and weekends included)
Tickets never expire once redeemed; Groupon voucher valid for 90 days from purchase
Save $3.26 per ticket vs. $16.08 national average – choose from 7 pricing options starting at $5.29
Multiple tickets can be redeemed in a single transaction for group bookings
Premium formats available with surcharge: 3D, IMAX, Dolby Cinema, and AMC Prime screens
Trusted by 25,000+ Groupon customers | Rated 4.7★ from 10,768 verified reviews
pricing_framing: Replace the unverifiable '38% savings' claim with concrete, fact-based value framing: 'Groupon price: $12.82 | National average ticket price: $16.08 (source: cabletv.com) | You save: $3.26 (20% below national average).' This approach uses the validated national market data from the research synthesis ($16.08 average) to make the savings claim verifiable and trustworthy, addressing the value_comm score of 5/10 and the AI flag for unverifiable discount claims. If AMC's direct box office price is available, display that instead for even stronger credibility.
executive_summary: The page scores 6.8/10 overall but has a critical trust issue: it claims 'Save Up to 38%' yet shows no original price anywhere (value communication: 5/10, AI flag, content gap #1). The #1 fix is to display verifiable savings using the $16.08 national average (actual savings: $3.26 = 20%), replacing the unverifiable 38% claim. The #2 fix is resolving contradictory fine print stating customers may pay more than box office admission, which directly undermines the value proposition. These two changes plus expanding the 68-char meta description to 155 chars could lift conversion 12–18%.

Remove all '38%' references until AMC's actual box office price can be displayed.

recommendations.short_title: Resolve contradictory fine print about higher prices
recommendations.recommendation: Rewrite or remove the fine print statement 'Depending on the time, date and location of redemption, the amount paid for these tickets may be higher than the posted box office admission price.' If this clause is legally required, add a clarifying sentence immediately after it explaining exactly when this applies (e.g., 'This applies only when using Yellow Tickets for premium formats like IMAX or 3D, which require a surcharge as noted above').
recommendations.current_state: Fine print states: 'Depending on the time, date and location of redemption, the amount paid for these tickets may be higher than the posted box office admission price. The difference will not be refunded and may not be applied to surcharges and/or upgrades.' No explanation is provided for when or why this would occur.
recommendations.proposed_state:
Yellow Ticket pricing is fixed at the amount you pay on Groupon and provides savings vs. standard box office admission for 2D movies. Premium formats (3D, IMAX, Dolby, AMC Prime) require an additional surcharge at the time of booking, which is paid separately and clearly displayed before you confirm your seats.

[If the original legal language must remain, append:] The above notice refers only to premium format surcharges, not to standard 2D admission.
recommendations.data_citation: AI flag: 'Contradictory fine print undermines value proposition: States amount paid may be higher than box office admission price without explaining when — directly contradicts the deal's savings claim'; content gap #4 cites this same issue
recommendations.impact_rationale: Removes a major trust barrier and value proposition contradiction that causes purchase hesitation and post-purchase regret; fine print that undermines the core benefit is a direct conversion killer.
supporting_evidence: AI flag identifies this as contradicting the deal's savings claim and potentially leaving customers feeling misled
Content gap #4 flags lack of explanation for when higher prices apply
Trust score is 9/10 (strong) but this clause works against that strength
